ledger.note: 1839: Kubang Pasu is created out of Kedah. 'The state was established in 1839 as a gift to Tunku Anum of the Kedahan nobility'; Sultan Ahmad Tajuddin 'rewarded Tunku Anum with 24 districts from Jitra to Sendawa'; first ruler Tunku Anum bin Tunku Abdul Rahman (1839-1853). The page gives the year and the district names but no outline.

ledger.note: 1839: the infobox lists Kubang Pasu as a 'Client state of Siam', without a date. The page's context is the Siamese occupation of Kedah after 1821 ('The Siamese Rattanakosin Kingdom successfully invaded Kedah in 1821') and Kedah's recovery of autonomy 'in 1842' on condition of tribute to Bangkok; the date of the clientage is not on the page, and 1839 (the founding) is taken as its start (page silent).

sources.title: Kingdom of Kubang Pasu Darul Qiyam
sources.note: Established 1839 as a gift to Tunku Anum from Sultan Ahmad Tajuddin; 24 districts from Jitra to Sendawa; client state of Siam (infobox); capital Kampung Pulau Pisang; reintegrated into Kedah in 1859; Siamese invasion of Kedah 1821, Kedah autonomy 1842.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch, as the state that took land out of Kedah between 1839 and 1859. One page opened (the English title 'Kubang Pasu' is a disambiguation page). Unsettled: (1) the outline: the page gives no area or boundary; the disc is an estimate, and Sendawa and the other districts are not located; the Kedah dossier and Cliopatria's Kedah shapes keep the land in Kedah throughout; (2) the Siamese clientage: the infobox says 'Client state of Siam' without a date; the vassal events are the researcher's reading (confidence 1 and 2); (3) the Kedah partition of 1843 is mentioned only in an infobox caption, so the page's own account of how Kubang Pasu relates to the Perlis separation of 1839-1842 (kedah-perlis-district) is not drawn; (4) the page does not mention 1909 or the Anglo-Siamese Treaty, and the kingdom ended in 1859 on the page; (5) a Malay militia offensive at Alor Ganu is undated on the page and not recorded; (6) the Kedah dossier has no loss for 1839 and no gain for 1859 (it would need both with this slug as counterpart). Gazetteer: none needed (coordinates only); Jitra, Pulau Pisang and Sendawa would be places.
